items.title: Authoritative document-state ownership is explicit
items.statement: The shared document store is expressly the sole text authority, all named LSP feature callers operate against it, workspace edits route through FileSafe, and LSP is denied ownership of Search, review, and chat restore semantics.

evidence.exact_quote: - the shared document store is the sole authority for open-document text
- workspace edits from rename/format/code action flow through the same FileSafe-backed mutation path as other file edits
- LSP never becomes the owner of Search, diff/review, or chat restore semantics

items.title: Stale feature requests have a stated synchronization barrier
items.statement: The plan explicitly requires sync barriers before feature requests and separately requires cancellation or discard on document-version changes; this closes the basic edited-buffer stale-result case, though it does not close restart-generation races identified separately.

evidence.exact_quote: - feature requests are gated behind sync barriers so stale document versions do not leak into the UI

| **Request timeout/cancellation** | Per-request timeout; cancel on navigate/edit | -- | Stale work abandoned | Timeout → treat as failure for that request (show "Timed out" or discard) | `lsp.*TimeoutMs` (§14.4) | N/A (client-side) |

items.title: Cached diagnostics can masquerade as current after timeout
items.statement: The timeout branch permits either last-known diagnostics or an empty set without defining freshness age, version binding, a stale badge, or the event that expires cached diagnostics. A user or Assistant can therefore act on obsolete diagnostics or interpret silence as health.
items.impact: Misleading Problems/editor state and incorrect Assistant fixes after edits, timeouts, or server degradation.

evidence.exact_quote: | **Diagnostics** | Buffer URI, open/change/close; server sends `publishDiagnostics` | Underlines, gutter markers, Problems panel rows | Errors/warnings shown; click opens file at line | Timeout: show last known or empty; server crash → clear diagnostics, offer "Restart"; no server → no diagnostics | `lsp.<id>.disabled`, `lsp: false` | No diagnostics; optional install hint |

items.title: User-visible lifecycle states lack a closed transition model
items.statement: The primary status contract exposes Initializing, Ready, Error, and None, while later metadata adds misconfigured and installing, but the plan never defines legal transitions, degraded or restarting states, terminal versus retryable errors, or which capabilities remain truthful in each state.
items.impact: The GUI, request broker, and Assistant context can disagree about attachment health and capability availability during install, restart, or partial initialization.

evidence.exact_quote: | **LSP status in UI** | Server state (Initializing/Ready/Error/None) | Status bar text or indicator | e.g. "Rust (rust-analyzer): Ready" | No server: show nothing (omit) | -- | Show nothing (omit) |

- Each effective `ServerSpec` records `language/extensions/selectors`, `/extensions/selectors`, `/files/conditions`, required markers/files/conditions, `context_exclude`, command `/env/init` options, `root-discovery` mode, optional platform restrictions, `/version` and `position-encoding` metadata, install `/provisioning` hints, and lifecycle status values for `/misconfigured/installing/error`.

items.title: Restart replay has no session-generation or completion barrier
items.statement: Crash restart replays documents, but the plan does not state how old-process responses and diagnostics are rejected, how concurrent edits are ordered against replay, or when the replacement session becomes request-capable. Document-version barriers alone do not distinguish two server process generations for the same URI and version.
items.impact: Late diagnostics or edits from a dead session can overwrite replacement-session truth, and requests can run before replay completes.

evidence.exact_quote: - Protocol guardrails are conservative by default: initialize -> initialized -> normal traffic -> shutdown -> exit is the strict lifecycle, dynamic registration stays disabled until PM can handle `/unregister`, and over-advertising unsupported snippets, resolve support, progress, `/code-action/workspace`, or workspaceFolders behavior is forbidden. Restart after `/crash` replays open documents, diagnostics are replacement-per-server plus URI rather than append-only, and rename, `/format/code-action`, and workspace edits always route through FileSafe.

items.title: Automatic server installation has no transactional trust contract
items.statement: The plan includes automatic downloads and many auto-installing catalog entries but does not specify artifact provenance, integrity or signature verification, destination and permissions, cancellation, interrupted-install recovery, rollback, cache cleanup, or offline behavior.
items.impact: A compromised or partial download could execute untrusted code or leave a server falsely reported as installed and usable.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Config:** `lsp` section in opencode config. Schema: `https://opencode.ai/config.json`. Per-server properties: `disabled` (boolean), `command` (string[]), `extensions` (string[]), `env` (object), `initialization` (object). Set `lsp: false` to disable all; set `OPENCODE_DISABLE_LSP_DOWNLOAD=true` to disable automatic LSP server downloads.
| astro | .astro | Auto-installs for Astro projects |

items.title: Custom server commands have no configuration trust boundary
items.statement: Arbitrary custom command arrays are supported, but the excerpt does not define whether project-controlled configuration is trusted, whether commands require user approval, what environment and filesystem access they receive, or how command-path substitution and inherited secrets are constrained.
items.impact: Opening an untrusted workspace could become a local code-execution or secret-exfiltration path if project configuration can select commands or environment values.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Custom servers:** Add entries with `command` (e.g. `["custom-lsp-server", "--stdio"]`) and `extensions`.

items.title: Server-rendered hover and diagnostic content lacks sanitization rules
items.statement: The plan correctly identifies server-returned payloads as dynamic external content, yet supplies no rendering trust model for Markdown, HTML, command links, images, oversized payloads, bidi controls, or control characters in hover, diagnostics, completion, and code-action labels.
items.impact: A malicious or compromised language server can spoof trusted UI, trigger unsafe links, degrade rendering, or conceal content.

evidence.exact_quote: **ELI5/Expert copy alignment:** Authored tooltip/help text in this plan (for example setting hints and UI explanatory copy) must follow the dual-variant contract in `Plans/FinalGUISpec.md` §7.4.0. LSP server-returned hover/diagnostic payloads are dynamic external content and are outside authored dual-copy enforcement.

items.title: Assistant diagnostics and telemetry have no data-lifecycle boundary
items.statement: Diagnostics and an optional telemetry snapshot may be attached to Assistant context, but the excerpt does not define user consent, local-versus-provider routing, secret or path redaction, file-scope minimization, retention, deletion, or whether remote-workspace data may cross hosts.
items.impact: Source paths, diagnostic text, code fragments, or PM telemetry may leave the intended host or persist beyond the user's expectation.

evidence.exact_quote: For Debug Mode, LSP diagnostics may be part of the structured context when the user points PM at a debug target, e.g. a local app, dev server, website, or other runnable surface. The Assistant-facing flow supports a Cursor-like loop from hypothesis to target evidence to workspace fix, and may attach a session `/telemetry` snapshot when it helps the chat agent reason about PM's own run.

items.title: Remote disconnect and reconnect semantics are absent
items.statement: Remote workspaces are required to use remote roots without a hidden local mirror, but there is no specified behavior for SSH loss, host-key change, path-map failure, reconnection, queued document changes, in-flight requests, stale diagnostics, or unsaved buffers while the host is unavailable.
items.impact: The editor can lose synchronization or present stale remote intelligence without a deterministic recovery path.

evidence.exact_quote: - remote-mode projects use remote host roots and MUST NOT silently attach against a hidden local mirror

items.title: Root identity lacks canonicalization and collision rules
items.statement: The session key and root-selection steps name root_identity but do not define canonicalization for symlinks, case-insensitive paths, UNC and drive-letter forms, remote path mappings, deleted or moved roots, nested worktrees, or two logical projects sharing the same physical path.
items.impact: Documents can attach to the wrong server process, duplicate processes can be spawned, or state can leak between projects and hosts.

evidence.exact_quote: - session reuse key is `(host_id, server_id, root_identity)`
- `root_identity` is resolved from the effective project/worktree/remote root selected for the current document and server rules

items.title: No enforceable resource limits exist for process and result growth
items.statement: One process is allowed per host, server, and root identity across a broad catalog, but no limits or backpressure rules cover concurrent processes, roots, open documents, diagnostic counts, workspace-symbol results, payload bytes, queue depth, CPU, memory, timeout storms, or eviction priority.
items.impact: Large monorepos or adversarial servers can exhaust memory, CPU, file descriptors, UI capacity, or Assistant context budgets.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Server model:** One LSP server **process** per **`(host_id, server_id, root_identity)`**. Root discovery still begins from the file context and server heuristics (e.g. "nearest directory containing Cargo.toml" for Rust), but the supervised session key is host-aware.

items.title: LSP visual surfaces have no accessibility contract
items.statement: Inline underlines, gutter markers, hover, completion, code lens, inlay hints, semantic colors, Problems rows, and status indicators are specified without keyboard-only operation, focus order, screen-reader names and announcements, non-color cues, zoom/reflow, reduced-motion behavior, or accessible error association.
items.impact: Core MVP language intelligence can be unavailable or misleading to keyboard, low-vision, color-blind, and screen-reader users.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Diagnostics:** Inline and gutter errors/warnings from language servers (replacing or augmenting the "placeholder for future linter/build errors" in FinalGUISpec).
- **LSP status in UI:** Status bar or indicator (e.g. "Rust (rust-analyzer)", "Initializing...", "Ready", "Error: ...").

items.title: Localization and text-layout behavior are unspecified
items.statement: Authored copy has an ELI5/Expert rule, but there is no locale selection, translation ownership, pluralization, RTL, long-string truncation, server-message language, filename and Unicode display, or fallback-locale contract for any LSP surface.
items.impact: Status, settings, Problems, and error flows can overflow or become inconsistent across locales, and dynamic server messages may mix languages unpredictably.

evidence.exact_quote: **ELI5/Expert copy alignment:** Authored tooltip/help text in this plan (for example setting hints and UI explanatory copy) must follow the dual-variant contract in `Plans/FinalGUISpec.md` §7.4.0. LSP server-returned hover/diagnostic payloads are dynamic external content and are outside authored dual-copy enforcement.

items.title: Protocol, toolchain, and persisted-config migration are not defined
items.statement: The plan pins LSP 3.17 as current and Slint tooling to 1.17.1, and records version and position-encoding metadata, but does not define supported version ranges, downgrade behavior, catalog/config schema migration, deprecated server IDs, encoding changes, or rollback when an upgrade breaks initialization.
items.impact: Existing projects and settings can silently change server selection or position mapping across upgrades, causing wrong edits and failed startup.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Protocol:** [Language Server Protocol](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/) (JSON-RPC 2.0). Current spec: 3.17.

- **Crate:** [slint-lsp](https://crates.io/crates/slint-lsp) (align with the Slint 1.17.1 toolchain target). LSP implementation for [Slint](https://slint.dev). Binary: `slint-lsp` (or `slint-lsp.exe` on Windows). Communicates via **stdio** (stdin/stdout); no special command-line arguments -- editors spawn the binary and use LSP over stdio.

items.title: Tracing is named without an operational support contract
items.statement: LspTraceService and tracing are implementation concepts, but the excerpt defines no event schema, correlation IDs across host/session/request/document version, health metrics, log levels, redaction, retention, support-bundle boundaries, user-visible diagnostic export, or success thresholds.
items.impact: Restart races, server-selection errors, privacy incidents, and performance failures cannot be reliably diagnosed or falsified in production.

evidence.exact_quote: - PM owns a client-pattern LSP orchestration layer rather than analyzer implementations. The live architecture names `LspHost`, `LspSupervisor`, `LspSession`, `LspSessionRegistry`, `LspRegistry`, `WorkspaceResolver`, `DocumentStore`, `DocumentSyncEngine`, `LspRequestBroker`, `CapabilityRegistry`, `DiagnosticsStore`, `LanguageIntelligenceFacade`, and `LspTraceService`; `/VS` or other upstream client examples are inputs only, while the GUI calls the `/intelligence` facade rather than JSON-RPC plumbing. `LspHost` also owns `/SSH` placement and `/path-mapping`, with all LSP/process I/O off the UI thread and delivered through an event-loop-safe handoff.

items.title: Executable LSP commands bypass the defined edit safety story
items.statement: Code lens is allowed to invoke actions, while the explicit FileSafe path covers workspace edits from code actions, rename, and formatting. There is no authority, preview, permission, cancellation, undo, or audit contract for `workspace/executeCommand` and command-bearing code lenses or completion items whose side effects are not representable as workspace edits.
items.impact: A language server command can run tests, tools, generators, or arbitrary mutations without the safeguards promised for FileSafe-backed edits.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Code lens:** Inline actionable links above symbols (`textDocument/codeLens`).

| **Code actions** | Range + diagnostics; user invokes | Context menu / lightbulb; apply edit | Edit applied via FileSafe | Timeout → hide actions; apply failure → show error, do not change buffer; no server → no code actions | -- | No code actions |

items.title: Mixed internal-tool LSP ownership is explicitly unresolved
items.statement: The plan itself states that mixed LSP actions remain under-owned until UI-session reads and mutation-capable apply-edit paths are separated. No caller, consumer, authority, or completion contract is supplied for that seam in this authoritative core.
items.impact: Tool events, UI reads, and mutation-capable LSP operations can be routed inconsistently or bypass policy enforcement.

evidence.exact_quote: - Internal-tool LSP boundaries are explicit: `LSPSupport.md` owns LSP `/tooling` behavior for plan-mode and `/interview` context, but `internal-tool` event records use `run_id`, `tool.invoked`, and `mutation_capable: bool`; mixed `lsp` actions remain under-owned until UI-session reads and mutation_capable apply-edit paths are separated.

items.title: Success prose is not a falsifiable acceptance oracle
items.statement: Feature success is described with outcomes such as 'Correct location/list' and 'Errors/warnings shown' but there are no executable fixtures, protocol transcripts, version-race tests, malformed-payload cases, accessibility checks, performance limits, or measurable pass thresholds for the MVP matrix.
items.impact: Implementations can claim conformance while disagreeing on correctness, latency, staleness, failure behavior, and UI truth.

evidence.exact_quote: | **Navigation** (go-to-def, outline, breadcrumbs) | (URI, position) or document; server capability | Jump to location or symbol list | Correct location/list | Timeout → show "Timed out", discard; no result → show "No definition"; no server → heuristic/outline | `lsp.workspaceSymbolTimeoutMs` (for workspace/symbol) | Heuristic symbol search, regex outline (FileManager §10.1-§10.2) |

items.title: Multi-server presentation preserves source identity
items.statement: The overlap model requires user-visible resolution, compatible-family checks, source-attributed code actions, and per-server diagnostic storage rather than flattening. This directly addresses the principal attribution and false-capability risk for multiple attached servers.

evidence.exact_quote: - effective overlap resolution must remain user-visible in Settings > LSP and status surfaces

- JavaScript-family overlaps generalize through `/typescript/eslint/oxlint-style` rules rather than one-off Deno/TypeScript/ESLint exceptions. Diagnostics merge only from compatible servers, and code actions from multiple servers are surfaced with source attribution so one server cannot silently override another.

items.title: Capability negotiation prohibits healthy-feature overclaiming
items.statement: The plan gates features on negotiated capabilities and explicitly forbids advertising unsupported client capabilities, providing a sound baseline against claiming semantic features a server or client cannot perform.

evidence.exact_quote: Capabilities are negotiated at **initialize**: client and server declare what they support; we only use features both sides advertise.

items.title: External protocol and catalog currency is intentionally unverified
items.statement: The excerpt asserts the current LSP specification and upstream server/tool facts, but capsule policy defers external research. Their present-day accuracy, licensing, platform support, and compatibility therefore remain unknown in this blind window rather than supportable gaps or confirmed non-gaps.
items.impact: Implementation choices may rely on upstream claims that have changed since the plan was authored.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Protocol:** [Language Server Protocol](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/) (JSON-RPC 2.0). Current spec: 3.17.

dimension_assessments.summary: Core editor consumers and document authority are named, but mixed internal-tool LSP reads and mutation-capable actions are explicitly under-owned.
Basic stale-request barriers exist, but the visible lifecycle vocabulary is inconsistent and has no closed transition or per-state capability model.
Edit-version synchronization is addressed, but restart generations and root-identity canonicalization leave late-message, replay-order, and session-isolation races.
Timeout, crash, and fallback cases are named, but diagnostic freshness, restart ordering, install interruption, remote loss, and resource exhaustion are not deterministic.
Open-document replay and FileSafe failure behavior exist, but there is no session-generation barrier, transactional installer rollback, remote reconnect policy, or upgrade rollback contract.
DocumentStore, FileSafe, GUI facade, and multi-server attribution are strong non-gaps, but custom commands, executable LSP actions, and internal-tool seams lack complete authority boundaries.
Assistant diagnostics, telemetry, traces, inherited command environments, and remote data have no consent, minimization, redaction, retention, or deletion contract.
Automatic downloads, custom commands, dynamic server-rendered content, and executable server actions lack a complete trust and validation model.
Capability negotiation and source attribution are explicit non-gaps, but cached diagnostics and the incomplete lifecycle state model can still masquerade as current or healthy.
No deterministic interrupted-download or remote-host disconnect and reconnect behavior is specified.
The per-host/server/root process model and broad catalog have no measurable quotas, backpressure, payload bounds, or eviction policy.
No keyboard, screen-reader, non-color, zoom, focus, or announcement requirements are supplied for the LSP GUI surfaces or dynamic payloads.
The dual-copy rule does not define localization, RTL, long-text, Unicode, or dynamic server-message language behavior.
Capability negotiation is addressed, but protocol/toolchain ranges, persisted schema migration, encoding change, downgrade, and rollback are absent; upstream currency is also unverified.
Tracing components are named without schemas, correlation, metrics, thresholds, redaction, retention, or support export, and resource limits lack monitoring or alerts.
FileSafe-backed workspace edits are an explicit non-gap, but custom commands and executable LSP commands have no equivalent permission, preview, undo, or audit boundary.
Root identity depends on project/worktree/remote owners and internal-tool mixed actions are expressly under-owned, leaving two material integration seams open.
No executable fixtures, malformed-input tests, race transcripts, accessibility checks, performance limits, or measurable acceptance thresholds ground the success prose.
External research is forbidden in this blind phase, so present-day protocol, catalog, licensing, platform, and dependency facts remain explicitly unknown.
